cues.zh: 但我想谈论量子力学的原因，你知道，老实说，是因为我写了一本关于量子力学的书，你现在就可以在 iPhone 上买

cues.zh: 都不用离开座位。但是，

cues.zh: 我认为这背后有个原因，而这个原因

cues.zh: 可以从我的加州理工学院前辈理查德·费曼的一句名言中推断出来。我想我可以有把握地说，没有人真正理解

cues.en: quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 量子力学。

cues.en: Now, I usually don't like to appeal to authority when I'm giving these lectures, but when the thing I'm trying to demonstrate is that physicists don't understand quantum mechanics, I'm allowed to appeal to someone who, if anyone, should have understood quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 通常我在做这些讲座时不喜欢诉诸权威，但当我要论证的是物理学家们并不理解量子力学时，我可以引用一位如果说有人应该理解量子力学、那非他莫属的人的话。

cues.zh: 像费曼这样的人说“没有人理解量子力学”，这到底是什么意思？他每天都在用量子力学。事实上，我们可以用量子力学做出极其

cues.zh: 精确的

cues.zh: 问题在于，我们理解

cues.zh: 量子力学并使用它的方式，和我使用我的iPhone完全一样。

cues.zh: 我可以发信号，我可以用应用，我可以发短信，甚至用手机给别人打电话。但如果你问，里面到底在发生什么？我怎么造一个这东西？细节是什么？

cues.zh: 我完全不知道。

cues.zh: 这就是专业物理学家与量子力学之间的关系。他们会用它，

cues.zh: 但如果你问他们底层到底在发生什么，他们会说，嗯，我们不知道。

cues.en: And that's perfectly fine when it's me and my phone. It's really embarrassing when it's physicists
cues.zh: 如果是我和我的手机，这完全没问题。但如果是物理学家

cues.en: and quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 和量子力学，那就真的很尴尬了。

cues.en: And the really bad thing is not just that physicists don't understand quantum mechanics. Not understanding is perfectly fine. Right? Not understanding drives science. We don't understand something, so we then try to understand it.
cues.zh: 而真正糟糕的不仅是物理学家不理解量子力学。不理解完全没问题，对吧？不理解推动科学前进。我们不理解某件事，于是才努力去理解它。

cues.en: The problem is that in the case of quantum mechanics, we don't even try anymore.
cues.zh: 问题在于，就量子力学而言，我们甚至不再尝试了。

cues.en: There was this time in the nineteen twenties and thirties when the greatest physics minds really thought deeply about what it means when quantum mechanical events happened, but then that was...
cues.zh: 在二十世纪二三十年代，最伟大的物理学头脑确实深入思考过量子力学事件发生时意味着什么，但后来那……

cues.en: That disappeared,
cues.zh: 那消失了，

cues.en: that project of trying to really deeply understand what's going on. It was thought to not be serious work. It was thought to be what one did at the end of one's career, or at the end of the day, there's a little brandy, you put on your smoking jacket, and you think about quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 那个试图真正深入理解到底发生了什么的研究计划。它被认为不是严肃的工作。人们认为那是一个人职业生涯末期才做的事，或者一天结束时，来点白兰地，穿上吸烟夹克，然后思考量子力学。

cues.en: It was not really what real physics is made of anymore.
cues.zh: 它不再真正是真正的物理学所包含的内容了。

cues.en: So if you ask many physicists today, like, what's really going on with quantum mechanics? They'll say, no, no, no, we don't care about that. We don't want to know.
cues.zh: 所以如果你问今天许多物理学家，比如，量子力学到底是怎么回事？他们会说，不不不，我们不关心那个。我们不想知道。

cues.en: So the metaphor, the parable
cues.zh: 所以我想借用的比喻、寓言

cues.en: that I'd like to borrow from is Aesop's fable
cues.zh: 是伊索寓言

cues.en: of the fox and the grapes. You know this one? The fox
cues.zh: 狐狸和葡萄。你知道这个吗？狐狸

cues.en: sees there's a nice juicy bunch of grapes up there, goes, oh, yes, I want these grapes. Fox jumps up and down to get the grapes, but the grapes are just out of reach, just a little bit too high.
cues.zh: 看到上面有一串美味多汁的葡萄，就说，哦，对，我想要这些葡萄。狐狸跳上跳下想够到葡萄，但葡萄刚好够不着，只是稍微太高了一点。

cues.en: So the fox says, you know what? I never wanted those grapes anyway. They're probably sour.
cues.zh: 狐狸说，你知道吗？那些葡萄我本来就不想要。它们八成是酸的。

cues.en: You're not supposed to explain your parables, but just to make things clear, the fox represents physicists.
cues.zh: 寓言本来不该解释，但为了让事情清楚点，狐狸代表的是物理学家。

cues.en: The grapes represent
cues.zh: 葡萄代表的是

cues.en: understanding quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 对量子力学的理解。

cues.en: Physicists tried, they failed, and now they've convinced themselves they never wanted to try. And I think that that's wrong, and that's embarrassing, and we should do better. So I have an idea, it's not my idea, I have a favorite version of quantum mechanics I would like to pitch to you, but much more important than my favorite version is the idea that we should be able to understand it. It's not mystery, it's not magic, it's just science.
cues.zh: 物理学家试过了，失败了，现在他们说服自己从来没想试过。我觉得这不对，这很丢人，我们应该做得更好。所以我有个想法，这不是我的原创想法，我有一个最喜欢的量子力学版本想推荐给你们，但比我最喜欢的版本更重要的是这个观念：我们应该能够理解它。它不是谜团，不是魔法，它就是科学。

cues.en: So let me remind you, where quantum mechanics came from, why we invented this whole scheme. You know, we started out in the sixteen hundreds with classical mechanics. Isaac Newton figured out the way the world worked according to a very simple set of rules, and this set of rules was so good, so compelling,
cues.zh: 让我提醒你们，量子力学从哪来的，我们为什么发明了这整套方案。你知道，我们从十七世纪的经典力学开始。Isaac Newton用一套非常简单的规则搞清楚了世界的运作方式，这套规则太好、太有说服力了，

cues.en: that the idea that classical mechanics was not right just never even entered people's minds. It was a framework in which you could do physics,
cues.zh: 以至于经典力学不对这个想法根本没进过人们的脑子。它是一个你可以做物理的框架，

cues.en: and everything else from electromagnetism
cues.zh: 而从电磁学到

cues.en: to Einstein's theory of general relativity
cues.zh: 爱因斯坦的广义相对论

cues.en: fit into the framework
cues.zh: 的一切

cues.en: of classical mechanics.
cues.zh: 都适配在经典力学的框架里。

cues.en: Quantum mechanics is something entirely
cues.zh: 量子力学是完全

cues.en: different. It's not an improvement on classical physics, it's a replacement, wholesale. Newton was wrong, quantum mechanics is saying something very different. And there's no place more vivid than that than this picture that you've all seen, the cartoon of an atom, the Rutherford atom. I love giving these talks in England because all these things happened in England. Right? And
cues.zh: 不同的东西。它不是经典物理的改进，而是彻底替换。Newton错了，量子力学说的是非常不同的事。没有比你们都见过的那张图更生动的了——原子的卡通图，Rutherford原子。我喜欢在英国做这些演讲，因为所有这些事都发生在英国。对吧？而且

cues.zh: Newton、经典力学、Rutherford在剑桥这里做了他的工作。

cues.zh: 但后来出现了这种李子布丁模型，认为原子是一大团模糊的东西，电荷分布在其中。

cues.zh: 是Rutherford证明那不对。原子的大部分质量集中在中心，在一个原子核里，

cues.zh: 这就是今天你看到的图景。对吧？我们都见过这张图。这个图

cues.zh: 或者材料中的电之类的东西。沉重的原子核只是待在那里，电子可以从一个原子跳到另一个原子。

cues.zh: 会有一个电场从它发出，所以如果我把电子移动一点，电场就会偏移指向电子所在的位置。所以如果我拿电子上下晃动，

cues.zh: 这意味着电子应该会损失能量。

cues.zh: 它不该待在稳定轨道上，而应该呈螺旋状向原子核中心靠近。

cues.zh: 这应该发生得非常快。你可以算一算，用数学证明电子从轨道坠入原子核中心大约只需要一百亿分之一秒。

cues.zh: 所以现在有一个我们都能参与的思想实验。我们可以问：这里有一张桌子，桌子里有原子；这里有你和我，我们也有原子。我预测，如果经典力学成立，一百亿分之一秒后，它们全都会坍缩成一个点。

cues.zh: 准备好了吗？开始。它并没有发生。所以

cues.zh: 经典力学存在深层次的问题。花了很长时间，很多聪明人以不同方式思考，才给出一个可能解释。他们提出的解释非常惊人，尽管花了不少时间，

cues.zh: 说实话，他们能这么快想出来已经很了不起了。这个解释就是：电子不是粒子。

cues.en: It's a pretty dramatic explanation, so I want it to sink in. Electrons are deep down,
cues.zh: 这个解释相当惊人，我想让它深入人心。电子从根本上说，

cues.en: they're really waves.
cues.zh: 其实是波。

cues.en: Rather than thinking about the electron as a little point moving in an orbit like a planet in the solar system,
cues.zh: 与其把电子想成一个像太阳系行星那样在轨道上运动的小点，

cues.en: you should think of the electron as a cloud, a wave like cloud
cues.zh: 而应该把电子想成一朵云，一朵像波的云

cues.en: concentrated
cues.zh: 集中

cues.en: near
cues.zh: 靠近

cues.zh: 原子核。至于那些被化学课折磨过的人，

cues.zh: 作为大学生，你们认得这些轨道，

cues.en: which are the different shapes that electron wave can take. Just like if you have a string that is tied down at both ends and you pluck it, there is sort of a fundamental frequency, then there are higher harmonics.
cues.zh: 它们是电子波可能呈现的不同形状。就像一根两端固定的弦，你一拨，会有一个基频，然后还有更高次谐波。

cues.zh: 所以电子不会螺旋坠入并坍缩到原子核中心的原因

cues.zh: 在房间后排举起手说，你们肯定不相信这个吧，但根本没人听他们的。所以我只想提这里非常非常明显的两个问题。一个是极其著名且被多次提及的，量子力学的测量问题。对吧？

cues.en: In those rules I taught you,
cues.zh: 在我教给你的那些规则中，

cues.en: there's a role played by observation or measurement, by looking at things.
cues.zh: 观察或测量，也就是看事物的过程，也起着作用。

cues.en: So the measurement problem is just,
cues.zh: 所以测量问题就是，

cues.en: what do you mean
cues.zh: 你是什么意思

cues.en: look at something?
cues.zh: 看点什么？

cues.en: Does it have to be a human being looking at it? Can the cat look at itself? Does that count?
cues.zh: 必须是人来看它吗？猫自己能看自己吗？那算数吗？

cues.en: What if it were not a cat? What if there was a video camera? What if we're an earthworm or an amoeba?
cues.zh:
要是它不是一只猫呢？
@@
要是有一个摄像机呢？
@@
如果我们是一只蚯蚓或是一个阿米巴原虫呢？

cues.en: What if I just glance at it?
cues.zh: 那我只瞄一眼呢？

cues.en: What do you mean a measurement? When does it happen? What qualifies as a measurement? How quickly does it happen? Is it instantaneous? Why is it probabilistic?
cues.zh:
你说的测量是什么意思？
@@
它是什么时候发生的？
@@
什么算作测量？
@@
这发生得有多快？
@@
它是瞬间完成的吗？
@@
为什么它是概率性的？

cues.en: And again, if you're in the back of the room in your quantum mechanics class and raise your hand and ask these questions, you're told not to ask these questions. You're not given sensible answers.
cues.zh: 话说回来，如果你坐在量子力学课的后排，举手问这些问题，别人会叫你别问，也给不出讲得通的回答。

cues.en: But there's an equally bad problem that I call the reality problem.
cues.zh: 但还有一个同样严重的问题，我称之为“实在性问题”。

cues.en: I said at the beginning, the electron is
cues.zh: 我一开始说过，电子是

cues.en: a wave, called the wave function.
cues.zh: 一种波，被称为波函数。

cues.en: But is it, really?
cues.zh: 但它真的是波吗？

cues.en: Because the whole point of those rules is that we never see the wave function. Whenever we look at the electron, it looks like a particle.
cues.zh: 因为那些规则的核心就在于，我们根本看不到波函数。只要我们去观察电子，它看起来就像是个粒子。

cues.en: Is the wave function really representing reality, or is it just a tool we use to predict
cues.zh: 波函数究竟代表着客观实在，还是仅仅是我们用来预测

cues.en: the outcomes of potential measurements we could do? Or do we need more than the wave function? Is wave function part of reality, but not all of reality? What is reality?
cues.zh: 潜在测量结果的一种工具？或者说，光有波函数还不够？波函数只是实在的一部分，而非全部？实在究竟是什么？

cues.en: We don't know.
cues.zh: 我们不知道。

cues.en: And this is why, in many discussions of quantum mechanics that physicists try to give to wide audiences,
cues.zh: 正因如此，物理学家在面向大众科普量子力学时，

cues.en: they get confused themselves.
cues.zh: 他们自己常常也越讲越糊涂。

cues.en: You know? Is the atom mostly empty space?
cues.zh: 你看，原子内部大部分是虚空吗？

cues.en: No, if you think the atom is mostly electron
cues.zh: 如果你认为原子大部分由电子

cues.en: wave function,
cues.zh: 波函数构成，那就不是；

cues.en: but yes, if you think the electron is secretly a particle inside the wave function. So we don't know the answer to these very, very basic easy to ask questions that should be embarrassing.
cues.zh: 但如果你认为电子其实是隐藏在波函数里的粒子，那它就是空的。所以我们连这些非常基础、张口就能问出的问题都答不上来，这理应让人感到惭愧。

cues.en: There's a long history, of course, of young people entering the field and saying, I'm going to answer these questions, and then being kicked out of the field.
cues.zh: 当然，历史上总有年轻人进入这个领域，撂下狠话说“我要解决这些问题”，结果却被直接扫地出门。

cues.en: One such person was Hugh Everett,
cues.zh: 其中有一位是 Hugh Everett，

cues.en: who in the 1950s
cues.zh: 他在 20 世纪 50 年代

cues.en: came up with what is called the Everett interpretation of quantum mechanics. He didn't call it that, but, you know.
cues.zh: 提出了后来所说的量子力学 Everett 诠释。他本人不这么称呼它，不过你懂的。

cues.en: And the wonderful thing is that Everett, in some sense, was being more of a therapist than a physicist.
cues.zh: 妙就妙在，从某种意义上说，Everett 与其说是物理学家，不如说更像一位治疗师。

cues.en: He
cues.zh: 他

cues.en: was giving away for physicists to accept reality
cues.zh: 是在帮助物理学家接受现实，

cues.en: in a way that they apparently were in denial about.
cues.zh: 而他们显然一直在否认现实。

cues.en: To these questions, what is reality? What happens at a measurement?
cues.zh: 对于这些问题：什么是现实？测量时会发生什么？

cues.en: He offers very simple answers. He says the wave function represents reality.
cues.zh: 他给出了非常简单的答案。他说，波函数代表现实。

cues.en: That's it. There's no extra stuff, and it's not just the tool to make predictions, it is
cues.zh: 就是这样。没有其他东西，波函数也不只是用来做预测的工具，它

cues.en: isomorphic
cues.zh: 与现实

cues.en: to reality. That's it.
cues.zh: 同构。就是这样。

cues.en: And what happens when you make a measurement? There's no collapse of the wave function. There's no sudden, unpredictable, probabilistic, stochastic thing. There's just the Schrodinger equation. Schrodinger equation applies
cues.zh: 测量时会发生什么？波函数不会坍缩。没有什么突然发生、无法预测、带有概率性的随机现象。只有薛定谔方程。薛定谔方程

cues.en: all the time
cues.zh: 始终

cues.en: to everything in the universe.
cues.zh: 适用于宇宙中的一切。

cues.en: Bold words indeed, but we already gave an argument that that can't be right. Right? Because the Schrodinger equation predicts the things coming out of the uranium should go in all directions, but we only see them go in trajectories.
cues.zh: 这话可真够大胆的，但我们已经论证过，这不可能是对的。对吧？因为薛定谔方程预测，铀原子里射出的粒子应该朝各个方向飞去，但我们看到的却只有沿着特定轨迹运动的粒子。

cues.en: But still, before we resolve that,
cues.zh: 不过，在解决这个问题之前，

cues.en: I do want to make it very clear how simple
cues.zh: 我确实想把这一点说清楚：这套理论

cues.en: this theory is. Right? Compared to the Schrodinger compared to the Copenhagen interpretation,
cues.zh: 有多简单。对吧？与薛定谔方程和哥本哈根诠释相比，

cues.en: the rules of Everettian quantum mechanics are beautifully simple.
cues.zh: Everett 量子力学的规则简单得令人惊叹。

cues.en: He just erases all of the rigmarole
cues.zh: 他直接抹掉了所有那些繁复的说辞

cues.en: about observations and measurements and collapses. He says there are wave functions, and they evolve according to the equation that you already know.
cues.zh: 关于观察、测量和坍缩。他说，波函数是客观存在的，它们就按照大家熟知的方程演化。

cues.en: He doesn't add anything at all to the formalism of quantum mechanics, he just takes things away.
cues.zh: 他完全没有给量子力学的数学形式增加任何东西，只是在做减法。

cues.en: The problem is,
cues.zh: 但问题在于，

cues.en: how in the world can this
cues.zh: 这到底该怎么

cues.en: map onto the reality that we see, map onto the reality that says when we look at electrons, they look like particles?
cues.zh: 对应到我们所见的现实？对应到那个“当我们观察电子时，它们看起来像粒子”的现实？

cues.en: So let's look at...
cues.zh: 我们来看一下……

cues.en: There's two things that Everett made use of
cues.zh: Everett 利用了两点，

cues.en: that
cues.zh: 它们

cues.en: absolutely part of quantum mechanics. He's just saying you should accept them.
cues.zh: 绝对属于量子力学本身。他只是说，大家应该接受它们。

cues.en: One is the fact that you are made of atoms, and therefore you
cues.zh: 其一，你是由原子构成的，因此你

cues.en: are part of the quantum world. You are not classical. That might be a nice approximation that works in certain circumstances,
cues.zh: 本身就是量子世界的一部分。你并不是经典物理对象。在某些特定情况下，经典物理可能是不错的近似，

cues.en: but honestly, the observer should be treated quantum mechanically just like the thing being observed.
cues.zh: 但说实话，观察者本身也应当像被观察的对象一样，用量子力学来对待。

cues.en: The other thing he makes use of is a phenomenon
cues.zh: 他利用的另一件事，是量子力学中

cues.en: of quantum mechanics called entanglement.
cues.zh: 一种被称为“纠缠”的现象。

cues.en: This was something that was really first emphasized by Einstein. Einstein, if anything,
cues.zh: 这其实最早是由 Einstein 重点强调的。真要说的话，Einstein

cues.en: is underrated.
cues.zh: 甚至被低估了。

cues.en: He's rated pretty highly. I know.
cues.zh: 我知道，大家对他的评价已经极高了。

cues.en: Man of the century. Right? Person of the century. But there's this reputation that by the time
cues.zh: “世纪伟人”，对吧？“世纪风云人物”。但人们总有一种看法，认为到了

cues.en: quantum mechanics was put together in the late nineteen twenties, there's literally a conference, the Solvay meeting in 1927,
cues.zh: 1920 年代末量子力学体系成型的时候——当时还真开过一次会，就是 1927 年的 Solvay 会议——

cues.en: where Einstein and Bohr and the others hashed out the rules of quantum mechanics, and there's this speech we give ourselves about how by that time Einstein was a little bit old, he was slowing down, he was too conservative, he couldn't keep up with the new physics.
cues.zh: Einstein、Bohr 等人在会上推敲敲定了量子力学的法则，而我们总习惯讲一套说辞：那时候 Einstein 已经有点老了，思维变慢了，思想太保守，跟不上物理学的新发展了。

cues.en: He was 48.
cues.zh: 他当时48岁。

cues.en: I do not want to admit
cues.zh: 我不想承认

cues.en: that at that age, one is too old to keep up with the latest advances.
cues.zh: 到了那个年纪，就太老了，跟不上最新的进展。

cues.en: The truth is that Einstein understood quantum mechanics better than anyone.
cues.zh: 事实是，爱因斯坦比任何人都更懂量子力学。

cues.en: The problem was he didn't accept it. He didn't think it was done. He didn't think that the Copenhagen interpretation was good enough. And one of the things he invented
cues.zh: 问题在于他不接受它。他不认为它已经完成。他不认为哥本哈根诠释足够好。而他发明的东西之一

cues.en: by thinking hard about it is this phenomenon of quantum entanglement.
cues.zh: 就是通过深入思考它，得出了量子纠缠这一现象。

cues.en: So I will illustrate it by thinking about the Higgs boson,
cues.zh: 所以我将通过思考希格斯玻色子来说明它，

cues.en: discovered just in 2012.
cues.zh: 它直到2012年才被发现。

cues.en: They didn't know about it in Einstein's time, but it's a nice illustration because other than the Higgs boson,
cues.zh: 爱因斯坦时代他们还不知道它，但这是一个很好的例子，因为除了希格斯玻色子之外，

cues.en: every particle, every fundamental particle that we know about in nature has what we call spin.
cues.zh: 我们所知的自然界中每一种粒子、每一种基本粒子都有我们所说的自旋。

cues.en: It rotates.
cues.zh: 它在旋转。

cues.en: And because of the rules of quantum mechanics, just like when you look at the cat inside the box, you never see it in a combination of awake and asleep,
cues.zh: 而由于量子力学的规则，就像你看盒子里的猫时，你永远不会看到它处于醒着和睡着的组合状态，

cues.en: An electron
cues.zh: 一个电子

cues.en: that is spinning,
cues.zh: 在自旋时，

cues.en: when you observe
cues.zh: 当你观察

cues.en: the spin,
cues.zh: 它的自旋，

cues.en: you always see it's either spinning clockwise, which we call spin up, or it's spinning counterclockwise,
cues.zh: 你总是看到它要么顺时针旋转，我们称之为自旋向上，要么逆时针旋转，

cues.en: which we call spin down. It's never actually any superposition
cues.zh: 我们称之为自旋向下。它实际上从来不是这两种可能性的

cues.en: of those two possibilities.
cues.zh: 叠加态。

cues.en: The rules of quantum mechanics say that when you're not looking at it, it is a superposition of those two possibilities.
cues.zh: 量子力学的规则说，当你不在看它时，它是这两种可能性的叠加态。

cues.en: The Higgs boson does not have any spin,
cues.zh: 希格斯玻色子没有任何自旋，

cues.en: but it can decay into two particles that are themselves spinning.
cues.zh: 但它可以衰变成两个本身具有自旋的粒子。

cues.en: And the nice thing about that is the total amount of spin in the universe stays the same when that happens.
cues.zh: 妙就妙在，发生这种情况时，宇宙的总自旋是保持不变的。

cues.en: So if a non spinning particle
cues.zh: 所以，如果一个没有自旋的粒子

cues.en: converts into two spinning particles,
cues.zh: 转化成了两个有自旋的粒子，

cues.en: you know
cues.zh: 你就会知道，

cues.en: that the two spinning particles have to be spinning in opposite directions,
cues.zh: 这两个粒子的自旋方向必定相反，

cues.en: so their spin cancels out.
cues.zh: 这样它们的自旋才能相互抵消。

cues.en: So here is the quantum mechanical prediction.
cues.zh: 量子力学的预测正是如此。

cues.en: The Higgs boson, with zero spin,
cues.zh: 自旋为零的 Higgs 玻色子，

cues.en: decays into two particles, a particle and an antiparticle.
cues.zh: 会衰变成两个粒子：一个粒子和一个反粒子。

cues.en: We don't know if we were to observe the spin of either particle what answer we would get.
cues.zh: 如果我们去观测其中任何一个粒子的自旋，事先并不知道会得到什么结果。

cues.en: But we do know if we observe the spin of one of the particles,
cues.zh: 但我们确切知道的是，只要测出其中一个粒子的自旋，

cues.en: the other one is opposite.
cues.zh: 另一个粒子的自旋必定相反。

cues.en: So the thing that the Higgs boson decays into by the rules of quantum mechanics is a combination of superposition
cues.zh: 因此，按照量子力学规律，Higgs 玻色子衰变后的产物实际上是一个叠加态：

cues.en: of particle one is spin up, particle two is spin down,
cues.zh: 粒子一自旋向上、粒子二自旋向下，

cues.en: plus particle one is spin down, particle two is spin up. There's no possibility if they're both spin up, that would violate the conservation of spin, the conservation of angular momentum. Okay?
cues.zh: 加上粒子一自旋向下、粒子二自旋向上。绝不可能两个都自旋向上，因为那会违反自旋守恒，即角动量守恒。懂了吗？

cues.en: So this just comes out of the need to preserve conservation of angular momentum,
cues.zh: 这纯粹是出于维持角动量守恒的需要，

cues.en: but it's a very profound thing. This is saying the following very, very big difference
cues.zh: 但它却极其深刻。它揭示了以下这个非常、非常巨大的差异——

cues.en: between classical mechanics and quantum mechanics. In classical mechanics, you have a bunch of particles,
cues.zh: 经典力学与量子力学之间的差异。在经典力学里，面对一堆粒子，

cues.en: and I could give you their states one by one. This particle is doing that, this other particle is doing the other thing.
cues.zh: 我可以逐个给出它们各自的状态：这个粒子在这样运动，另一个粒子在那样运动。

cues.en: You might think that for quantum particles,
cues.zh: 你可能会以为，对于量子粒子，

cues.en: they each have a wave function.
cues.zh: 它们各自都有一个波函数。

cues.en: Particle one is some combination of spin up and spin down, so is particle two.
cues.zh: 粒子一是自旋向上和自旋向下的某种组合，粒子二也一样。

cues.en: But no, that is not how it works.
cues.zh: 但不对，事情不是这样的。

cues.en: There are not separate wave functions for every bit of the universe. There is only one wave function, whatever it called the universal wave function,
cues.zh: 宇宙的每个部分并没有单独的波函数。只有一个波函数，不管它叫什么——就是所谓的通用波函数，

cues.en: what Stephen Hawking calls the wave function of the universe.
cues.zh: 也就是 Stephen Hawking 所说的宇宙波函数。

cues.en: And according to the wave function of the universe, these two particles are related, they are entangled.
cues.zh: 而根据宇宙波函数，这两个粒子是相互关联的，它们是纠缠的。

cues.en: We don't know what answer we will get if we measure the spin of particle one,
cues.zh: 我们不知道测量粒子一的自旋会得到什么结果，

cues.en: but we know that it will be the opposite of the spin of particle two.
cues.zh: 但我们知道，它会是粒子二自旋的反向。

cues.en: This is something that they didn't really know about in the nineteen twenties, but Einstein and his friends pointed out in the nineteen thirties,
cues.zh: 1920年代人们还不太了解这一点，但Einstein和他的朋友们在1930年代指出了它，

cues.en: and it wasn't until twenty years later that Hugh Everett put it to work to understand the measurement problem. So here is the Schrodinger's cat experiment
cues.zh: 直到二十年后，Hugh Everett才用它来理解测量问题。所以，下面是Everett版本下的薛定谔的猫实验

cues.en: according to Everett.
cues.zh: 按照 Everett 的说法。

cues.en: There is only one wave function, the wave function of the universe, and you are part of it.
cues.zh: 只有一个波函数，即宇宙波函数，而你也是它的一部分。

cues.en: So now the observer
cues.zh: 所以现在，观察者

cues.en: is in parentheses,
cues.zh: 被放在括号里，

cues.en: the observer is a quantum system, the role of the observer is now being played by Hugh Everett,
cues.zh: 观察者是一个量子系统，观察者的角色现在由 Hugh Everett 来扮演，

cues.en: and we're not going to have any magical wave function collapses, etc. All we're going to do is run the equation, the Schrodinger equation. You and I obey the Schrodinger equation just like electrons
cues.zh: 我们不会搞任何神奇的波函数坍缩之类的东西。我们要做的只是运行方程，也就是薛定谔方程。你和我就像电子一样遵守薛定谔方程

cues.en: and cats.
cues.zh: 和猫。

cues.en: So when you open the box,
cues.zh: 所以当你打开盒子时，

cues.en: there's nothing mystical, nothing magical, nothing sudden. There is an interaction,
cues.zh: 没有什么神秘、没有什么魔法、也没有什么突然发生。有的是一种相互作用，

cues.en: a physical relationship that comes into being between the observer and the thing being observed,
cues.zh: 一种在观察者和被观察对象之间产生的物理关系，

cues.en: and that entangles
cues.zh: 并且它使

cues.en: those two things.
cues.zh: 这两个东西发生纠缠。

cues.en: So it is absolutely unambiguous that the Schrodinger equation says
cues.zh: 所以薛定谔方程说得非常明确：

cues.en: that what you get when you open the box is a superposition
cues.zh: 你打开盒子后得到的是一个叠加态，

cues.en: that is entangled
cues.zh: 它是纠缠的，

cues.en: such that the cat's awake and the observer saw it awake,
cues.zh: 使得猫醒着，而观察者看到它醒着，

cues.en: or the cat's asleep and the observer saw it asleep. Everyone agrees. That's what the equation predicts.
cues.zh: 或者猫睡着，而观察者看到它睡着。大家都同意。这就是方程的预测。

cues.en: The problem is
cues.zh: 问题在于，

cues.en: no one has ever entered, opened a box, looked inside, and felt like
cues.zh: 从来没有人进去、打开盒子、往里看，然后感觉自己

cues.en: they're in a superposition of having seen the cat awake and having seen the cat asleep. No one has ever felt like they're in a superposition of having seen the electron spin up and spin down.
cues.zh: 处于“看到猫醒着”和“看到猫睡着”的叠加态。也从没有人感觉自己处于“看到电子自旋向上”和“看到电子自旋向下”的叠加态。

cues.en: So it's not that this makes no sense mathematically,
cues.zh: 所以并不是这在数学上说不通，

cues.en: the claim is this is not the world. This is not the world that we experience.
cues.zh: 关键在于，这不是真实世界。这不是我们经验到的世界。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好吗？

cues.en: How, mister Everett, are you going to map this very beautiful theory onto reality?

cues.zh: 即便我说“我们”，指的也是专业物理学家，那些高薪的聪明人。对吧？我们所有人的直觉基本上都建立在经典力学之上。你看，我们认为有某种叫“桌子”的东西，而且它在空间中有一个确定的位置。

cues.en: Very old fashioned to think that.
cues.zh: 这种想法其实非常陈旧。

cues.en: And nevertheless, that's how we talk.
cues.zh: 可尽管如此，我们平时还是习惯这么说。

cues.en: And it extends to how we develop new theories
cues.zh: 这种思维甚至延伸到了我们如何构建

cues.en: of stuff in the universe, whether it's the electromagnetic
cues.zh: 关于宇宙万物的新理论，无论是电磁

cues.en: field, or quarks, or oscillators,
cues.zh: 场、夸克还是振子，

cues.en: or whatever, we start with a classical theory,
cues.zh: 或者随便什么东西，我们都是先从经典理论入手，

cues.en: and then we quantize it. We try to promote that classical theory to a quantum mechanical theory.
cues.zh: 然后对其进行量子化。我们试图把经典理论提升为量子力学理论。

cues.en: The problem is
cues.zh: 但问题在于，

cues.en: nature doesn't do that. Nature doesn't start with a classical theory and then quantize it. Presumably, nature just is quantum from the start, and classical mechanics is some approximation,
cues.zh: 大自然并不是这么干的。大自然不会先搞一套经典理论再去量子化。推测大自然从一开始就是量子的，而经典力学只是一种近似，

cues.en: some limit,
cues.zh: 某种极限，

cues.en: some version of a very narrow
cues.zh: 是现实世界中极其狭窄的一隅，

cues.en: part of reality that works pretty well in certain very specific circumstances.
cues.zh: 只是在某些非常特定的情况下十分好用。

cues.en: So therefore,
cues.zh: 因此，

cues.en: there's no reason why
cues.zh: 没有任何理由认为，

cues.en: this procedure of starting with a classical theory and quantizing it
cues.zh: 这种“先从经典理论出发再去量子化”的做法

cues.en: must work
cues.zh: 就一定

cues.en: all the time. Maybe when the things that we're trying to understand are very subtle
cues.zh: 永远行得通。也许当我们试图理解的事物极其微妙

cues.en: and nuanced,
cues.zh: 且精细时，

cues.en: you have to start with the quantum description from the beginning
cues.zh: 你必须从一开始就采用量子描述，

cues.en: and then find the classical description as an approximation
cues.zh: 然后再设法把经典描述

cues.en: to it somehow.
cues.zh: 作为它的某种近似推导出来。

cues.en: That's a job that is perfectly suited for the many worlds interpretation
cues.zh: 这项工作非常适合多世界诠释

cues.en: of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 量子力学中的多世界诠释。

cues.en: The many worlds interpretation talks about wave functions and the Schrodinger equation. It talks about entanglement
cues.zh: 多世界诠释讨论波函数和薛定谔方程。它还讨论纠缠

cues.en: and evolution through time, purely quantum mechanical
cues.zh: 以及随时间的演化，这些纯粹是量子力学的

cues.en: notions.
cues.zh: 概念。

cues.en: You can put in classical notions like positions and momenta if you want, but they are not intrinsic to the theory. Unlike every other version of quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 如果你愿意，可以引入位置和动量之类的经典概念，但它们不是这个理论的内在要素。与量子力学的其他所有版本不同，

cues.en: it doesn't rely on any pre existing classical baggage.
cues.zh: 它不依赖任何预先存在的经典包袱。

cues.en: So let's see if we can't make a little bit of progress on a hard problem.
cues.zh: 所以看看我们能不能在一个难题上取得一点进展。

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 比如，

cues.en: quantum gravity
cues.zh: 量子引力

cues.en: is a hard problem.
cues.zh: 就是个难题。

cues.en: What does that mean, quantum gravity? Here's Einstein again.
cues.zh: 量子引力是什么意思？又说到 Einstein。

cues.en: Everyone shows you pictures of Einstein in his later years, where the hair was big and grey, and he was wearing a rumpled sweater. But back in the day, when he was inventing relativity,
cues.zh: 大家给你看的 Einstein 照片都是他晚年，头发又大又灰，穿着皱巴巴的毛衣。但当年他发明相对论时，

cues.en: he was a well dressed young man, and someone was combing his hair.
cues.zh: 他是个衣着考究的年轻人，还有人在给他梳头。

cues.en: And he had these wonderful ideas, special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity, nineteen o five, he kind of weds space and time together.
cues.zh: 他提出了这些绝妙的想法：狭义相对论和广义相对论。狭义相对论，1905年，他算是把空间和时间结合在了一起。

cues.en: The speed of light is an absolute maximum. I think there's an upcoming royal institution lecture about the speed of light. Right? Gets rid of the ether and so forth.
cues.zh: 光速是绝对上限。我记得皇家研究院即将有一场关于光速的讲座。对吧？它摆脱了以太等等。

cues.en: Ten years later, in general relativity,
cues.zh: 十年后，在广义相对论中，

cues.en: he says, you know, this space time thing, this four dimensional place where we live, has a life of its own. It's dynamical. It can be curved and bent. And you and I perceive and interpret that curvature of space time as gravity.
cues.zh: 他说，你知道，时空这玩意儿，我们居住的这个四维场所，有自己的生命。它是动态的。它可以弯曲和扭曲。而你我把时空的这种曲率感知并解释为引力。

cues.en: The reason, according to Einstein, why apples fall from trees is because the Earth
cues.zh: 据爱因斯坦所说，苹果从树上掉落的原因，是因为地球

cues.en: exerts a force on space time itself
cues.zh: 对时空本身施加了一种力

cues.en: to curve space time so that apples want to naturally fall if the tree is not holding them up. So this is a wonderfully successful
cues.zh: 使时空弯曲，于是如果树没托住苹果，苹果自然会往下落。所以这是一个极为成功的

cues.en: theory of gravity
cues.zh: 引力理论

cues.en: that fits perfectly into the classical Newtonian paradigm.
cues.zh: 完美契合了经典的牛顿范式。

cues.en: It's different than Newton's laws of physics,
cues.zh: 它不同于牛顿的物理定律，

cues.en: but it fits into that world where in principle, have a
cues.zh: 但它融入了那个世界——原则上，有一个

cues.en: something, the curvature of space time, there's an equation
cues.zh: 东西，时空的曲率，有一个方程

cues.en: cleverly called Einstein's equation
cues.zh: 巧妙地叫做爱因斯坦方程

cues.en: that tells you how space time curvature evolves
cues.zh: 告诉你时空曲率如何

cues.en: over time. There's nothing quantum mechanical about it.
cues.zh: 随时间演化。这里面没有任何量子力学的成分。

cues.en: But of course, we also have quantum mechanics, so we want to reconcile
cues.zh: 但当然，我们还有量子力学，所以我们想调和

cues.en: general relativity with quantum mechanics. That's the goal of quantum gravity.
cues.zh: 广义相对论与量子力学。这就是量子引力的目标。

cues.en: Now, for every other force of nature that we know about,
cues.zh: 那么，对于我们已知的其他每一种自然力，

cues.en: electromagnetism
cues.zh: 电磁力

cues.en: or the little nuclear forces,
cues.zh: 或者那些小的核力，

cues.en: the Higgs boson, the electrons and the quarks,
cues.zh: 希格斯玻色子、电子和夸克，

cues.en: this idea of starting with the classical theory and quantizing it works pretty well.
cues.zh: 这种从经典理论出发再对其进行量子化的思路，效果相当不错。

cues.en: It hasn't always been easy. Right? Richard Feynman won his Nobel Prize for quantizing electromagnetism.
cues.zh: 这并不总是容易的。对吧？理查德·费曼因为量子化电磁力而获得了诺贝尔奖。

cues.en: It took a lot of real brainpower to do that, but still, eventually, you get the right answer.
cues.zh: 这需要大量的真才实学才能做到，但最终你还是能得到正确答案。

cues.en: For gravity,
cues.zh: 对于引力，

cues.en: we fail.
cues.zh: 我们失败了。

cues.en: If you try to quantize general relativity, you get nonsense.
cues.zh: 如果你试图量子化广义相对论，你会得到荒谬的结果。

cues.en: Quantities that should be finite numbers are infinite, you don't even know what the terms mean, it's just kind of a mess. So I would like to suggest
cues.zh: 本应是有限数值的量变成了无穷大，你甚至不知道那些项是什么意思，就是一团糟。所以我想提出

cues.en: that's because we've been doing the wrong thing. I need to mention one more thing. There's the motto at the bottom there,
cues.zh: 那是因为我们一直在做错事。我需要再提一点。底部那里有一句箴言，

cues.en: geometry is related to energy. This is the very, very simple essence
cues.zh: 几何与能量相关。这就是广义相对论

cues.en: of general relativity. The geometry of space time is influenced by, and in turns influences back,
cues.zh: 非常非常简单的本质。时空的几何受到

cues.en: the energy of the stuff within it.
cues.zh: 其中物质能量的影响，反过来也影响它。

cues.en: So to turn that into a quantum theory, what I want to suggest is that maybe you shouldn't be
cues.zh: 所以，要把它变成量子理论，我想提出的是，也许你不应该

cues.en: quantizing gravity.
cues.zh: 把引力量子化。

cues.en: Maybe what you should be trying to do is to find gravity within
cues.zh: 也许你该做的是，在

cues.en: quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 量子力学中，

cues.en: within the wave function of the universe.
cues.zh: 在宇宙的波函数中寻找引力。

cues.en: I mean, after all,
cues.zh: 我的意思是，毕竟，

cues.en: we say, oh, we have not been able to understand quantum gravity,
cues.zh: 我们说，哦，我们一直没能理解量子引力，

cues.en: but then we admit we don't even understand quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 但接着我们又承认，我们连量子力学都不理解。

cues.en: What right do we have to think that we should be able to understand quantum gravity? So let's try something new.
cues.zh: 我们凭什么认为自己应该能理解量子引力？所以，让我们尝试点新东西。

cues.en: Now, when we do this, we are allowed to sort of cheat just a little bit by using features of the world that we do understand and that we do know. Well, one thing we know is that when we forget about gravity,
cues.zh: 现在，当我们这样做时，我们可以稍微“作弊”一下，利用我们确实理解、确实知道的世界的特性。嗯，我们知道的一件事是，当我们忽略引力，

cues.en: and just think about the other forces and particles of nature,
cues.zh: 只考虑自然界的其他力和粒子时，

cues.en: the best way we have of describing them is this framework called quantum field theory.
cues.zh: 我们描述它们的最佳方式就是这个叫量子场论的框架。

cues.en: All the talk that I've been giving you about electrons and protons and particles
cues.zh: 我之前跟你们讲的关于电子、质子和粒子的所有内容

cues.en: is kind of just an approximation
cues.zh: 其实只是一种近似，

cues.en: to the real underlying thing, which are quantum fields.
cues.zh: 近似于真正底层的东西，也就是量子场。

cues.en: And we're in the right place to talk about that. The person more responsible than anyone else for saying the world is... To start starting the idea that fields are fundamental was Michael Faraday with the electric
cues.zh: 我们现在正好适合谈这个。在提出场是基本的概念上，功劳最大的人是迈克尔·法拉第，他提出了电场

cues.en: and magnetic fields.
cues.zh: 和磁场。

cues.en: So here's a magnet. Right? You put the magnet, and if you don't put any iron filings around it, it's just empty space outside, but you and I know there's secretly a magnetic field everywhere around the magnet.
cues.zh: 这里有一块磁铁。对吧？你放上磁铁，如果周围不撒铁屑，外面看起来就是空无一物，但你我都知道，磁铁周围其实处处都隐藏着磁场。

cues.en: In modern quantum field theory,
cues.zh: 在现代量子场论中，

cues.en: what we say is that literally everything, not just forces like electricity and magnetism,
cues.zh: 我们说的是，实际上一切事物，不仅仅是电和磁这样的力，

cues.en: but even matter particles like electrons and neutrinos and quarks are really part of vibrating
cues.zh: 但即便是电子、中微子和夸克这类物质粒子，其实也是振动的一部分

cues.en: fields
cues.zh: 字段

cues.en: that fill all of space.
cues.zh: 填满整个空间。

cues.en: So that's a big change in perspective from a particle based view, at least when it comes to the nature of empty space.
cues.zh: 所以，与基于粒子的视角相比，这是一个视角上的重大转变，至少在涉及虚空本质时是如此。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好的？

cues.en: In a particle view,
cues.zh: 从粒子的视角来看，

cues.en: you have particles that have locations,
cues.zh: 你有一些带有位置的粒子，

cues.en: and then in between the particles, there's nothing but empty space. Okay? There's nothing going on. Empty space is boring.
cues.zh: 然后，在粒子之间，除了空无一物的空间，什么都没有。对吧？那里什么都没发生。空无一物的空间很无聊。

cues.en: Whereas in the field based view,
cues.zh: 而在基于场的视角下，

cues.en: a particle is just a way of talking about a field vibrating
cues.zh: 粒子不过是谈论场在振动的一种方式

cues.en: more than it does in empty space.
cues.zh: 比在真空中更甚。

cues.en: But even empty space, the fields are there,
cues.zh: 但即使是在太空中，场也依然存在，

cues.en: they're just in their lowest energy state. They're doing the minimal thing it's possible to do.
cues.zh: 它们只是处于最低能量状态。它们在做可能做到的最少的事情。

cues.en: So we talk about modes, the different vibrational frequencies of the quantum fields.
cues.zh: 所以我们讨论模式，也就是量子场不同的振动频率。

cues.en: Even in the emptiest region of empty space, there's an electron field, a magnetic field, an electric field, a gravitational field.
cues.zh: 即使在空无一物的空间中最空旷的区域，也存在电子场、磁场、电场、引力场。

cues.en: All of them have a certain quantum state.
cues.zh: 它们都有特定的量子态。

cues.en: Those modes of the fields are doing something.
cues.zh: 这些字段模式正在发挥作用。

cues.en: What they're doing is looking like empty space.
cues.zh: 它们所做的事，就是看起来像空无一物的空间。

cues.en: But they're there, and that's very important.
cues.zh: 但它们确实存在，这非常重要。

cues.en: Because what that lets us do
cues.zh: 因为这样能让我们

cues.en: is talk about the entanglement
cues.zh: 谈论纠缠

cues.en: of those different fields. Remember, we don't... If we're being quantum first, we don't have a lot of words to work with,
cues.zh: 也就是那些不同场之间的纠缠。记住，我们并不……如果从量子出发，我们可用的词并不多，

cues.en: but one of the words we have is entanglement.
cues.zh: 但我们可以用的词里，有一个就是纠缠。

cues.en: Okay? So you will not be surprised to hear
cues.zh: 听明白了？所以听到下面这一点你也不会意外：

cues.en: that if you have different regions of empty space with different vibrating quantum fields in them,
cues.zh: 如果不同的真空区域中有不同的量子场在振动，

cues.en: those fields will be entangled with each other, and guess what? The closer they are to each other, the more entangled they are.
cues.zh: 这些场之间就会产生纠缠，而且你猜怎么着？它们靠得越近，纠缠就越深。

cues.en: So if you start with empty space and you have a geometry,
cues.zh: 所以如果你从真空出发，并且拥有某种几何结构，

cues.en: whether it's Euclidean or Riemannian, whatever you want, whatever level of sophistication you've reached, it will be the case that the empty space parts of the quantum fields have a very simple relationship.
cues.zh: 不管是欧氏几何还是黎曼几何，随你怎么选，无论多么复杂，真空中量子场之间的关系其实都非常简单。

cues.en: You know how close things are just by measuring their entanglement and vice versa.
cues.zh: 只要测量它们的纠缠程度，就能知道距离有多近，反之亦然。

cues.en: So the idea,
cues.zh: 所以这个想法，

cues.en: the proposal, the suggestion,
cues.zh: 这个提议，这个建议，

cues.en: the guess, the hypothesis,
cues.zh: 这个猜想，这个假设，

cues.en: is that we can reverse that.
cues.zh: 就是我们可以把这个逻辑倒过来。

cues.en: Rather than saying the closer the areas
cues.zh: 与其说区域靠得

cues.en: are,
cues.zh: 越近，

cues.en: the more entangled they are, we can say the more entangled
cues.zh: 纠缠就越深，不如说

cues.en: these bits of the quantum field are, the closer they are.
cues.zh: 量子场的这些部分纠缠得越深，它们就靠得越近。

cues.en: We will define what it means to be nearby
cues.zh: 我们把所谓的“近”，

cues.en: to mean highly entangled.
cues.zh: 定义为“高度纠缠”。

cues.en: And we will define what it means to be far away to be not very entangled.
cues.zh: 把所谓的“远”，定义为“弱纠缠”。

cues.en: Okay? So what we're doing here
cues.zh: 明白了吗？所以我们在这里做的事情，

cues.en: is asking whether space itself
cues.zh: 就是探究空间本身，

cues.en: and the geometry of space, right, distances and angles and all that stuff,
cues.zh: 以及空间的几何结构，比如距离、角度等等，

cues.en: can emerge in some natural way
cues.zh: 能否以某种自然的方式涌现出来，

cues.en: from a quantum wave function that does not have space built into it from the start.
cues.zh: 脱胎于一个一开始并不包含空间概念的量子波函数。

cues.en: And the answer is yes.
cues.zh: 而答案是肯定的。

cues.en: If the wave function has certain properties, if the entanglement structure works out in a certain way,
cues.zh: 只要波函数具备某些特定性质，纠缠结构满足某种规律，

cues.en: you can map that quantum wave function and say, oh, this is three-dimensional space.
cues.zh: 你就能映射那个量子波函数并得出结论：看，这就是三维空间。

cues.en: A different quantum wave function would represent five dimensional space, or a two dimensional plane with different amounts of curvature and so forth.
cues.zh: 不同的量子波函数会代表五维空间，或是带有不同曲率量的二维平面等等。

cues.en: So as it shows on the top, there's a relationship
cues.zh: 所以正如顶部所示，存在着一种关系

cues.en: between geometry of space and the entanglement of quantum fields in that space.
cues.zh: 介于空间的几何结构与空间中量子场的纠缠之间。

cues.en: Meanwhile,
cues.zh: 同时，

cues.en: there's also a relationship between the entanglement of the fields and the energy
cues.zh: 场的纠缠与它们所具有的能量之间

cues.en: that they have. In this picture I showed you right here, there are no particles. This is literally supposed to represent empty space.
cues.zh: 也存在一种关系。我在这里向你展示的这幅图景中，没有粒子。这实际上代表的是空无一物的空间。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好吧？

cues.en: Let's put some particles in it. What does that mean in this language? That means we take the quantum fields and we vibrate them a little bit,
cues.zh: 让我们在其中放入一些粒子。用这种语言来说意味着什么？意味着我们取量子场，让它们轻微振动一下，

cues.en: and what that does is it breaks the entanglement
cues.zh: 而这样做会打破

cues.en: between that little vibrational mode in that region of space and everything around it.
cues.zh: 该空间区域中那个微小振动模式与周围一切之间的纠缠。

cues.en: So by decreasing
cues.zh: 所以通过减少

cues.en: the entanglement,
cues.zh: 纠缠，

cues.en: we did something that we know in our intuition
cues.zh: 我们做了某件事，而凭直觉我们知道

cues.en: is equivalent to putting energy
cues.zh: 这等价于向系统中

cues.en: in the system by putting a particle there. If you add a bunch of particles until you made a table,
cues.zh: 注入能量，也就是在那里放一个粒子。如果你不断添加粒子，直到造出一张桌子，

cues.en: you would have to break a lot of the entanglement of the vacuum modes of this region of space with the region around it. And in fact, you can make this into equations. Again, employment
cues.zh: 你就必须打破该空间区域真空模式与周围区域之间大量的纠缠。而事实上，你可以把它写成方程。再一次，这活儿

cues.en: for graduate students at Caltech,
cues.zh: 是给加州理工学院的研究生干的，

cues.en: figuring out how to relate the amount of entanglement in a region of empty space to the amount of energy that you would perceive being there.
